primary_diagnosis: Acute Upper Gastrointestinal Hemorrhage Secondary to Bleeding Gastric / Peptic Ulcer
secondary_diagnoses: Refractory Peptic Ulcer Disease (Rule out H. pylori resistance / NSAID use)
clinical_reasoning: Patient with endoscopic confirmation of gastric ulcer 4 months ago now presents with classic melena (black tarry stool) and hematochezia, signaling brisk acute upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage. This is a life-threatening complication requiring emergency inpatient stabilization, hemodynamic monitoring, intravenous proton pump inhibitors, and urgent therapeutic endoscopy.
recommended_tests: Emergency Diagnostic & Therapeutic Upper GI Endoscopy (EGD)
Serial Complete Blood Count (CBC) & Hematocrit Monitoring
Blood Grouping, Typing, and Crossmatch for immediate PRBC transfusion
Coagulation Profile (PT/INR, aPTT) and Serum Electrolytes
